## Run

In the LTEE project, Nextflow is in the `pipeline` environment: put
`pixi run -e pipeline` in front of each command (or use the task:
`pixi run run-nextflow`). Always launch from the project folder.

| What you want | Command |
|------------|------------------------|
| Run the workflow with the shared settings file | `nextflow run workflow/nextflow/main.nf -params-file config/config.yaml` |
| Reuse the tasks that already finished | add `-resume` |
| Change one parameter | add `--min_depth 10` (two dashes: a workflow parameter) |
| Write the results somewhere else | add `-output-dir results/nextflow-d10` (one dash: a Nextflow option) |
| An HTML report of the run | add `-with-report results/nextflow/execution-report.html` |
| Check the code | `nextflow lint workflow/nextflow/` |
| Which version | `nextflow -version` |
| Past runs | `nextflow log` |
| Delete the work files of older runs | `nextflow clean -f -before RUN_NAME` |
| Run an nf-core pipeline | `nextflow run nf-core/demo -r 1.2.0 -profile test,docker --outdir DIR` |

See [lesson 10, sections 3, 6 and 8](../pages/10-nextflow.qmd#run-the-finished-pipeline).

## When a task fails

Every task runs in its own folder under `work/`; Nextflow prints it when a
task fails. Go there and read:

| File | What it holds |
|------------|------------------------|
| `.command.sh` | the exact command the task ran |
| `.command.err`, `.command.log` | its error messages and log |

Run `bash .command.sh` in that folder to repeat the error by hand. See
[section 5](../pages/10-nextflow.qmd#look-at-a-task).

*Task requirement exceeds available CPUs*: a process asks for more CPUs
than the computer has. In `nextflow.config`, inside `process {}`:
`resourceLimits = [cpus: Runtime.runtime.availableProcessors()]` lowers the
request instead. See [troubleshooting](../pages/10-nextflow.qmd#troubleshooting).

## A process

```{.groovy}
process ALIGN {
    tag "${sample}"
    cpus 4

    input:
    tuple val(sample), path(reads)
    tuple path(genome), path(index)
    val bwa_extra

    output:
    tuple val(sample), path("${sample}.aligned.sorted.bam"), path("${sample}.aligned.sorted.bam.bai")

    script:
    """
    bwa mem -t ${task.cpus} ${bwa_extra} ${genome} ${reads[0]} ${reads[1]} > ${sample}.aligned.sam
    samtools sort -o ${sample}.aligned.sorted.bam ...
    """
}
```

## The workflow: channels in, channels out

```{.groovy}
workflow {
    main:
    ch_samples = channel.fromPath(params.samples)
        .splitCsv(header: true, sep: '\t')
        .map { row -> tuple(row.sample, [file(row.fastq_1), file(row.fastq_2)]) }
    ch_bam = ALIGN(ch_samples, ch_reference, params.bwa_extra)

    publish:
    bam = ch_bam
}

output {
    bam {
        path 'bam'      // below the output folder
    }
}
```

| Write | What it does |
|------------|------------------------|
| `params { min_depth: Integer = 2 }` | a parameter with a type and default; `params.min_depth` reads it |
| `channel.fromPath(FILE)` | a channel with one file |
| `channel.fromList([2, 5, 10])` | a channel with one item per value |
| `.splitCsv(header: true, sep: '\t')` | one item per row of a sample sheet |
| `.map { row -> ... }` | change each item |
| `.collect()` | all items as one list (for example, all FastQC files for MultiQC) |
| `.combine(other)` | every pair of items from two channels |
| `.mix(other)` | both channels' items in one channel |
| `publish:` and `output { }` | which results are saved, and where |

See [sections 1 and 6](../pages/10-nextflow.qmd#processes-channels-outputs-a-toy).

## Official cheat sheets and references

Nextflow has no official cheat sheet. The closest official references, in
the Nextflow documentation (now hosted by Seqera):

- Nextflow, *CLI reference* (every command and option): <https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/cli>
- Nextflow, *Syntax* (the language, in one page): <https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/syntax>
- Nextflow documentation: <https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/>
- Nextflow training, from the Nextflow team: <https://training.nextflow.io/>
